newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE euroyen ends thin trade up on JGB gains.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE euroyen ends thin trade up on JGB gains.

text.p: Key March three-month euroyen interest rate futures settled higher on Tuesday in line with the key Japanese government bond (JGB) futures contract rising to four-month highs.

But trade was subdued as operators were cautious about buying further from the current high levels. Traders said a stiff barrier lay at 99.29-99.30. The March ended at 99.28 after rising to 99.29, the highest intraday since February 10.
The level of 99.29 was the March contract's lifetime high, but turnover was only 20,185 contracts.

"Since the March is approaching a ceiling, operators are interested in a flattening in short-term interest rates. That means they are buying distant months like the June contract," said a city bank dealer.
The June contract settled the day session up 0.03 at 99.14 in turnover of 2,0791 contracts.
When the June's turnover of night and day sessions exceeds that of the March, the market will consider the June the new benchmark contract, traders said.

"Whether the JGBs' uptrend will continues this week is a question mark prior to a series of corporate straights to be launched later in the week and next week's 10-year JGB auction," the city bank dealer said.

The BOJ conducted a neutral money market operation for a second day Tuesday, draining 100 billion yen from the market. Key overnight call money was mainly traded at 0.48 percent, unchanged from Monday. Around 20 billion yen of key three-month certificates of deposit (CDs) were issued at 0.57 percent, the rate being unchanged from Monday.--Tokyo newsroom (813) 3432-8570; email: tokyo.newsroom@reuters.com
